title: Approve a wave as one action: approve every waiting run in order and stop at the first failure
lead: *Proposed.* One command (`ork approve WAVE-ID`) and one key approve every run of a wave that waits on approval, one after the other in start order, and stop at the first run that does not land. No human check is skipped. The scope, the human-check handling and the key are open owner questions.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Friction found in the v1.1 prescan (2026-10-31, friction 4). With pair waves (two relays at once in two worktrees, then landed one after the other; owner, 2026-10-31), each run has its own approval card, its own human checks and its own `a`. Landing is serial in any case: the engines of a project share one lock, `engine.Landings`, and the next landing waits and reads the base branch the first one moved (`internal/engine/landlock.go:11-62`; `docs/design.md:395-398`). So the owner approves A, waits for it to land, then approves B. The wait between the two is the owner's, not the machine's.

Today (facts read on 2026-10-31):
- `run.approve` returns once the run rests again, which includes the landing or its fix round (`ownerRunReply`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:913-1049`; `docs/design.md:1265-1268`: "`run.approve` returns the run record once the run rests again (S148)"). A landed run has `landed_at`; a blocked landing comes back to `awaiting-approval` with `land_fixes` above 0.
- `Engine.Approve` refuses while any human check is open (`internal/engine/engine.go:383-396`).
- `ork stop` takes a run or a wave by the `wave-` prefix (`internal/cli/run.go:227-233`; adj 138 `wave.stop-target`, decided prefix). `ork approve RUN` takes one run only and asks no confirmation (`ownerCommand`, `internal/cli/run.go:207-262`). The TUI asks `y/N` on an Overview row and approves with one key in the card (`internal/tui/model.go:1560-1581`).
- The wave id is on every run record (`Wave`, `internal/runrec/record.go:261`) but not on the engine run rows the TUI reads (`source.EngineRun`, `internal/source/source.go:230-260`), so the TUI cannot yet tell which runs share a wave.

Slicer check: `slicer find "approve all"` and `slicer find "batch approve"` return nothing in ork's roadmap. Approval is ork's (`landing.in-ork`, adj 162).

Open owner questions (MANIFEST-E.md, AW-Q1 to AW-Q4). The Implement steps use the recommended answers and name where an answer changes them.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
E-class: this slice touches `internal/daemon` and, for the TUI part, source.EngineRun. At most one E-class slice per wave. It is M; if the work runs over one Codex run, split it into the daemon and CLI part and the TUI part (the second depends on the first).

- `internal/daemon/waveapprove.go` (new): wave.approve handler and result types.
- `internal/daemon/waveapprove_test.go` (new).
- `internal/daemon/wire.go:21-24` (method constant and types), `internal/daemon/handlers.go:81-92` (dispatch), `internal/daemon/client.go` (client method).
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:1243-1345` (engineRuns: add Wave to the row) and `internal/source/source.go:230-262` (EngineRun.Wave, omitempty, *proposed*).
- `internal/cli/run.go:207-262` (ork approve takes a wave- id as ork stop does), `internal/cli/cli.go:55` (usage line) and :247 (dispatch), and `internal/cli/s17_test.go`.
- `internal/tui/keys.go:60-124` and :411-470 (the key and hint), `internal/tui/model.go:1480-1600` (requestAction, actionRefusal, the confirm), `internal/tui/live.go:15-35` and `internal/tui/daemon.go` (a WaveApprove method), `internal/tui/live_test.go:24` (fakeLive), `internal/tui/actions_test.go`.
- `testdata/golden/` (a confirm prompt golden, new) and `docs/dashboard.md` (Overview actions, the approval card section ~:900-1000).
- `docs/design.md:96-120` (method table), :1086-1110 (CLI list), :1198-1205 and :1262-1280 (approve text), `docs/guide.md` section 10 (:317-362), `docs/state.md` only if it gains a field.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under ## Unreleased, marked *proposed*).

Pair planning: E-class; keep it out of a wave with another E-class slice. Its TUI part shares `internal/tui/model.go` and `docs/dashboard.md` with most UI slices, so pair it with an N-class slice that avoids them (for example a docs-only slice).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
`internal/daemon/waveapprove_test.go` (the method does not exist: `unknown_method`; the fixtures are runs created through `wave.start` and moved to `awaiting-approval` as in `internal/daemon/approval_test.go`):
- `TestWaveApproveApprovesEachWaitingRunInStartOrder`: three members, all awaiting approval, all human checks marked: they are approved one at a time in `created_at` order, each only after the previous run rests again; the result lists each with outcome `landed`.
- `TestWaveApproveStopsAtTheFirstRunThatDoesNotLand`: the second member's landing goes to a fix round (back to `awaiting-approval` with `land_fixes` 1): the third is not approved and is reported `not-attempted`, and the first stays `landed`.
- `TestWaveApproveStopsAtAnApproveError`: `Engine.Approve` returns an error for the second member (for example the slicer note write fails): the third is untouched; the error is on the second item.
- `TestWaveApproveRefusesWhenAnyHumanCheckIsOpenAndApprovesNothing` (AW-Q2 answer a): the refusal names each run and its open checks, code `refused`, and no run was approved.
- `TestWaveApproveNeverMarksOrSkipsAHumanCheck`: the call changes no `human_checks` state and writes no `run.check`.
- `TestWaveApproveLeavesRunsThatAreNotWaiting`: a member still in `implement`, `queued` or `paused` is not approved and is listed with its state; a committed member is listed as done.
- `TestWaveApproveWithNoWaitingMemberIsRefused`: `refused`, text says no run of the wave awaits approval.
- `TestWaveApproveUnknownWaveIsNotFound` and `TestWaveApproveNeedsTheWavePrefix` (`bad_params`, like `stopWave`).
- `TestWaveApproveStopAfterCommitCountsAsDone`: a member with `stop_after` `commit` ends `committed` and counts as success (outcome `committed`).
- `TestWaveApproveStopsWhenTheCallIsCancelledBetweenRuns`: cancelling the context after the first member leaves the rest unapproved; the in-flight approval finishes.
- `TestEngineRunRowsCarryTheWave` (daemon): `engine_runs` rows have `wave`.

`internal/cli`:
- `TestApproveWaveIDApprovesTheWave`: `ork approve wave-...` calls `wave.approve` and prints one line per member (`ITEM RUN OUTCOME`); exit 1 when any member failed or was not attempted; `--json` prints the result.
- `TestApproveRunIDStillApprovesOneRun`: unchanged behavior for a run id.

`internal/tui`:
- `TestWaveApproveKeyAsksFirstAndListsTheOrder`: the key on a row whose run belongs to a wave with at least one other waiting run opens a confirm naming the items in order (`Approve and land A, then B? [y/N] (Enter is No)`), calls nothing until `y`.
- `TestWaveApproveKeyIsRefusedWhileAnyCheckIsOpen`: the status line names the run and its open checks (AW-Q2 answer a); nothing is called.
- `TestWaveApproveKeyIsHiddenWhenTheWaveHasOneWaitingRun`: the plain `a` stays the way to approve one run.
- `TestWaveApproveStatusReportsEachOutcome`: after the call the status reads `landed A, B` or `landed A; B needs a fix round; C not approved`.
- Golden `pane-approval-...` or Overview confirm prompt at 100x30 and 80x24 (mono).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first. Do not touch: `Engine.Approve`, the landing (`land`), the `Landings` lock, human-check marking, `run.approve`'s behavior for a single run, or the `a` key's meaning.

1. Preflight: AW-Q1 to AW-Q4 are answered. Defaults below are the recommended answers; change the named step if the owner chose otherwise.
2. Daemon: `wave.approve` params `{wave}` (a `wave-` id; scope per AW-Q1). Read the members from the run store and the live engines, as `stopWave` does (`internal/daemon/runs.go:714-760`). Order: `created_at` ascending, then run id (start order; AW-Q3 alternative: order of reaching approval). Pre-validate (AW-Q2 a): if any waiting member has an open human check, refuse the whole call with `refused` and name each run and check (reuse `openChecks`, `internal/engine/approval.go:82`), approving nothing. Then loop: for each member in `awaiting-approval`, call the same path as `run.approve` (`d.ownerRunReply(ctx, MethodRunApprove, ...)`) and wait for it to rest. Success is a record in `committed`. Anything else (an error, `awaiting-approval` again, `paused`, `stopped`) ends the loop; the rest are reported `not-attempted`. Check `ctx.Err()` between members. The result is *proposed*: `{"wave","items":[{"item","run","outcome","error"?,"state"}]}` with outcome one of `landed`, `committed`, `failed`, `not-attempted`, `not-waiting`, `done`.
3. `source.EngineRun.Wave` and the `engineRuns` row.
4. CLI: `ork approve RUN|WAVE`: a first argument starting `wave-` calls `wave.approve`. No confirmation prompt, as `ork approve RUN` has none today (the command is the confirm); print one line per member. Exit 1 if any member is `failed` or `not-attempted`.
5. TUI: the key per AW-Q4 (recommended: `A`, shift-a, if the keymap check below finds it free on the Overview and Running views; `A` is used only by Decisions and Waves, `internal/tui/keys.go:60`). It acts on the wave of the selected run, only when that wave has two or more members waiting on approval and no open check. It asks `y/N` like the Overview approval (`model.go:1577-1581`), names the items in order and says the approval lands and cleans up each (S119, adj 162, adj 152). One `WaveApprove` call per confirm, in a command, never in `Update`.
6. Docs, *proposed*: `docs/design.md` (method, CLI line, a paragraph in the approve text), `docs/dashboard.md` (the key, the confirm, the status wording), `docs/guide.md` section 10 (when to use it, that it stops at the first failure and never ticks a check).
7. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`: `Approve a wave in order (*proposed*): ...`. Add it as the final edit so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.

UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/tui ./internal/source`.
- `rg -n 'WithKeys\("A"' internal/tui/keys.go` shows the one existing binding (Decisions and Waves); the new key must not collide in the Overview, Running or pane contexts.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] With a real pair wave of two small slices, both at `awaiting-approval`: tick every human check, press the key, read the confirm at 100x30 and 80x24, confirm, and watch the first land and then the second. Then repeat with a pair whose second landing hits a conflict and confirm the first lands, the second goes to a fix round, and nothing else is approved.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Approve a wave in order: ork approve WAVE-ID and one key, stop at the first failure".
